source.title: Phase diagram and eigenvalue dynamics of stochastic gradient descent in multilayer neural networks
source.authors: Chanju Park; B. Lucini; Gert Aarts

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the reported study.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies how stochastic gradient training succeeds or fails under different hyperparameters, but uses synthetic teacher-student regression and reports test loss and other training observables rather than benchmark training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper does not report CIFAR classification or training classification error. Its own regression results on test loss and training observables bear on training success, but none of the versions specifies this synthetic teacher-student setup or these measures. The paper also discusses cited prior work; those cited findings are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests the initialization-dependent learning-efficiency part of V4 in a new setting: a shallow tanh teacher-student regression network with one trainable matrix. Small initial variance avoids tanh saturation and permits successful learning; large variance produces small initial gradients and slow, jammed learning. It does not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors additionally argue that spectral dynamics and approximate phase boundaries help explain the regimes and guide hyperparameter selection; they recommend small initial variance and the largest temperature remaining within the successful-learning region.
record.recipe_differences: Synthetic teacher-student regression with tanh activations and MSE; only the intermediate weight matrix is trainable, while first and final student matrices are fixed to teacher matrices. Reports test loss and training observables, not benchmark training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with learning-rate-to-batch-size ratio and initial weight variance; higher temperature and larger initial variance are associated with poor learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing learning-rate-to-batch-size ratio produces fluctuation-dominated nonconvergence, including with small initial variance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this fixed-batch tanh regression setup, learning fails above a temperature-dependent transition.

fits_no_version.finding: Feature memory, target alignment, and weight-spectrum dynamics distinguish successful, jammed, and high-temperature regimes; a spectral signal-to-noise criterion approximately tracks their boundaries.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature and weight-spectrum observables characterize SGD training regimes in this single-trainable-matrix teacher-student model.

record.problems: The study uses a relatively small synthetic teacher-student regression network and trains only one weight matrix; it does not use realistic datasets or classification error. Error bars are omitted from Fig. 3, and many results are presented as phase-diagram figures without exact per-condition values in the text. The authors identify extension to realistic data and deeper or wider networks as future work.

untested.parts: CIFAR convolutional classification, training classification error, corrupted labels, model-size comparisons, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU spurious local minima, joint teacher-student scaling, and extra student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, batch-normalized convolutional networks, very deep plain tanh networks, and Fixup.

Signal and gradient propagation across increasing depth, maximum trainable depth, activation-function comparisons, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and very deep convolutional networks. No quantitative time-to-target comparison is reported.
Initial linearized stability limits, transient loss recovery, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence from below that threshold.
Batch normalization versus no normalization, learning-rate tolerance attributable to normalization, and Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record excludes V4 too broadly: testing initialization-dependent learning efficiency does not require also testing depth or orthogonal weights. Evidence here is qualitative and restricted to a shallow network with only one trainable matrix; these untested extensions do not warrant scope-limiting verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test classification training error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, or model size and stopping comparisons.
Does not study two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima or vary student width relative to teacher width.
Does not compare plain and residual networks, depth, batch normalization, or Fixup.
Varies initial weight variance, but does not compare activation-matched initialization schemes, orthogonal and Gaussian weights, or trainable depth.
Varies learning-rate-to-batch-size ratio, but does not test rates relative to a stability threshold or measure the catapult mechanism or edge-of-stability behavior.
Does not compare batch normalization with no normalization or test Fixup.

rows.operation_detail: Tracked eigenvalues of X = W(2)W(2)T during training in three selected hyperparameter settings.
rows.measure: Eigenvalue dynamics; stochastic fluctuations widen the distribution and eigenvalues grow, potentially reaching a gradient-vanishing point.
rows.note: The text describes this as high-temperature dynamics; no numerical eigenvalue outcomes are stated outside the figure.
rows.check: Weight eigenvalue growth is not loss curvature and does not establish V5's stability threshold or catapult mechanism.

rows.subject: hyperbolic-tangent teacher-student network (ensemble of 100 models)
rows.size_stated: input 3; hidden layers 32 and 16; scalar output; L=3
rows.operation_detail: Tracked eigenvalues of X = W(2)W(2)T during training in three selected hyperparameter settings.
rows.measure: Eigenvalue dynamics; initial distribution is broad and eigenvalues evolve slowly without converging.
rows.note: The paper identifies this as jamming-phase behavior.
rows.check: Slow weight-spectrum evolution is a mechanistic correlate; the direct initialization-dependent learning evidence is already represented by R2 and R5.

rows.subject: hyperbolic-tangent teacher-student network (ensemble of 100 models)
rows.size_stated: input 3; hidden layers 32 and 16; scalar output; L=3
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated a convergence criterion based on the average eigenvalue level spacing for ensembles across the phase diagram.
rows.measure: Fraction of runs satisfying the estimated convergence inequality; boundaries are described as tracking the transition region, with the 2σ and 3σ boundaries capturing the ordered phase well.
rows.note: This is a convergence criterion for eigenvalue dynamics, not training classification error. The paper states that the criterion tracks the transition especially well for time correlation and that the higher-sigma boundaries capture the ordered region.
rows.check: This evaluates the study's spectral convergence criterion, not a claim version. The percentages are selected contour thresholds, not uncertainty estimates or independently reported success rates. Equation (4.15) is written as a divergence inequality, although the surrounding text describes satisfying it as convergence; this sign inconsistency needs clarification.

relationships.condition: Low-temperature tanh teacher-student regression, varying the Gaussian initialization variance of the sole trainable intermediate matrix.
relationships.reason: R1, R2, and R5 show efficient learning with small variance and slow, jammed learning with large variance, consistent with avoiding activation saturation and vanishing gradients.
relationships.display_finding: Small Gaussian initialization variance enabled efficient learning, whereas large variance produced slow, jammed learning associated with saturation and vanishing gradients.
